note: The camping area is beside the Wet Glaize Creek canoe-access lot, at the end of a 400 m gravel lane north off Route A: a boulder-ringed gravel lot of about ten cars with a picnic spot, and the designated camping ground in open timber just east of it. No built pads, so a rig stays on the lot. No toilets or water. Creek bottom ground that floods. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC designates a primitive camping point beside the creek-access lot (map symbol + GIS point) - stays under the lot rule, rig on the lot. Phone matches. Free/FCFS/14 nights/no hookups confirmed. PIN: move 58 m from woods onto the lot.
flags: LOT RULE - STAYS (designated point beside a lot): the page lists 'Designated Camping Sites'; the 12/19/2023 map legend has 'Primitive Camping' and draws that symbol with the Picnic Area symbol immediately east of the P at the end of the lane off Route A, on the south bank of Wet Glaize Creek; GIS layer 27 has one 'Primitive Camping Area' point at 37.99829,-92.51335, 58 m east of that lot's GIS point. The brochure (12/2021): 'Camping is allowed anytime in designated camping areas. These may or may not have defined campsites.' and 'The area offers a 10-car parking lot off State Road A for canoe access to Wet Glaize Creek ... Toilet facilities or potable water are not provided.' Imagery (leaf-off, 0.33 m/px): an oval gravel lot about 27 x 30 m ringed with boulders at the end of a single-lane gravel drive about 400 m long through old fields; a small grassy opening with cedars east of the lot, then open bottomland timber where the GIS point falls. No pads, rings, tables or privy can be seen, and the boulders keep vehicles on the gravel, so a motorhome camps on the lot itself with the camping ground a walk of 20-60 m. It is the Lick Creek case (designated point at a lot), not a bare lot.
PIN MOVE: stored 37.99829,-92.51335 (the GIS point) is in timber 58 m east of the lot. Move to the lot: 37.99825,-92.51402.

WATER: Wet Glaize Creek (15-20 m wide here) runs about 50 m north of the lot through leaf-off timber, with the canoe access between. Stored not waterfront stands (creek seen only through standing timber; day-use access between).

ACCESS: paved Route A, then the 400 m gravel lane; no ford, no posted limit, no 4WD wording. The other four lots (Route A west end, two on the gravel road north of the creek, one on Route C) carry no camping symbol.
BROCHURE: 'No unattended camp fires.' No campsite seasons ('Camping is allowed anytime').
PHONE: stored 573-346-2210 matches the page's 'For more information call (573) 346-2210' (brochure: Camdenton District, same number).
Nothing else in the database within 3 km. No split (one camping point).
